views.name: cards_base_projection
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  asciiName,
  artist,
  setCode,
  number,
  rarity,
  type,
  types,
  subtypes,
  supertypes,
  manaCost,
  convertedManaCost,
  faceConvertedManaCost,
  colors,
  colorIdentity,
  colorIndicator,
  availability,
  borderColor,
  layout,
  frameVersion,
  text,
  originalText,
  flavorText,
  power,
  toughness,
  loyalty,
  edhrecRank,
  isReprint,
  isPromo,
  isOnlineOnly,
  hasFoil,
  hasNonFoil,
  isFullArt,
  isAlternative,
  isTimeshifted,
  mtgjsonV4Id,
  scryfallId,
  mtgoId,
  mtgoFoilId,
  multiverseId,
  mcmId,
  cardKingdomId,
  purchaseUrls,
  printings
FROM cards

params.description: A normalized, one-row-per-card projection of the cards table exposing identifying, descriptive, and collectible attributes for each card (grain = id).
params.when_to_use: Lookup detailed card attributes by card id or uuid | Filter cards by setCode, name, rarity, type, colors, or other card-level attributes | Base projection to join with set, legality, printing, price, or language-specific views while preserving card-level uniqueness | Compose further aggregations or metrics per card (e.g., counts of printings, available purchase links) by joining to exploded/aggregated siblings appropriately

params.metric: No aggregated measures are defined in this projection (grain = cards.id). All columns are passthrough attributes from cards. If you need counts or aggregates, compute them after joining to one-to-many sources and aggregating back to this card.id key. Example derived metric patterns that can be composed on top of this view: | printings_count = COUNT(distinct card_printings.printing_id) GROUP BY cards.id | available_purchase_sources = COUNT(distinct purchase_table.source) GROUP BY cards.id | min_price = MIN(prices.price) GROUP BY cards.id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to set or set-level views on setCode — join to sets on cards.setCode = sets.code is safe because cards rows are one-per-card-printing (id) and sets is one-row-per-set; this will not duplicate card-level attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_color_identity_exploded on cards.id = cards_color_identity_exploded.id is NOT safe for naive SELECT * because cards_color_identity_exploded is one-to-many (one card -> multiple exploded color_identity rows). To preserve card-level measures, aggregate the exploded view back to cards.id (e.g., string_agg or array_agg) before joining, or join and then re-aggregate. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to card_legalities_current on cards.id = card_legalities_current.id is safe if card_legalities_current is a one-row-per-card (it is documented as AGG — check it returns one row per card). If card_legalities_current contains multiple rows per card for different formats, you must aggregate or filter to a single format before joining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: do NOT join directly to card_rulings_latest or card_foreign_latest_per_language without ensuring they are one-row-per-card; these views are RANK-based and may be one-to-many (per language or multiple rulings). Either join on a composite key that guarantees one row (e.g., id + language + rank = 1), or aggregate their rows to cards.id first (e.g., latest_ruling_text = MIN/ARRAY_AGG filtered to latest). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: joining to cards_edhrec_rank_running (WIN) may be unsafe if it contains multiple time-series rows per card. Aggregate or filter to the desired partition (latest) before joining to avoid multiplying rows/metrics. | General rule: This projection is one-row-per-cards.id. Any join to a dimension that is also one-row-per-key (set metadata, canonical card metadata keyed by id or uuid) will not duplicate rows. Any join to tables/views that are one-to-many (printings list, exploded color identity, rulings, foreign translations, price history) WILL multiply rows unless those tables are pre-aggregated or the join includes a deterministic single-row filter (e.g., latest per language). When composing metrics, always GROUP BY cards.id after joining one-to-many sources or perform subquery aggregation keyed by cards.id before joining.

views.description: Normalized projection of the cards table preserving key identifiers and exposing commonly used descriptive and measure columns. Useful as a base relation for joins, filtering cohorts, and analytics that need card-level attributes without modifying original column names. | Use for: list cards with specific attributes (rarity, setCode, colors); base card metadata for joining to legalities/sets/foreign_data; filter and aggregate card measures like convertedManaCost or edhrecRank

views.name: cards_with_set
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.uuid,
  c.name,
  c.setCode,
  c.number,
  c.rarity,
  c.type,
  c.colors,
  c.convertedManaCost,
  c.edhrecRank,
  s.id AS id_1,
  s.code,
  s.name AS name_1,
  s.block,
  s.type AS type_1,
  s.releaseDate,
  s.baseSetSize,
  s.totalSetSize
FROM cards c
LEFT JOIN sets s
  ON c.setCode = s.code

params.description: Provides one row per card (cards.id) enriched with its set record where available — useful for card-level reporting with set attributes.
params.when_to_use: Fetch card details together with the set the card belongs to (set metadata like name, release date, sizes). | Filter or group cards by set attributes (set code, set name, block, releaseDate) while keeping card-level grain. | Join card-level measures (counts, prices, edhrecRank) to set metadata for display or aggregation. | As a building block for composing further card-level queries that need set context without rejoining sets.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the view — cards.id from table cards (one row per card). | uuid: cards.uuid — card unique identifier (likely a GUID) from cards.uuid. | name: cards.name — card name from cards.name. | setCode: cards.setCode — set code on the card (FK-ish) from cards.setCode used to join to sets.code. | number: cards.number — the collector number on the card from cards.number. | rarity: cards.rarity — rarity text from cards.rarity. | type: cards.type — card type line from cards.type. | colors: cards.colors — card colors representation from cards.colors. | convertedManaCost: cards.convertedManaCost — numeric converted mana cost from cards.convertedManaCost. | edhrecRank: cards.edhrecRank — numeric EDHREC popularity rank from cards.edhrecRank. | id_1: sets.id — the set's internal id (renamed id_1 in the SELECT) from sets.id. | code: sets.code — set code from sets.code (same values as cards.setCode when joined). | name_1: sets.name — set name (renamed name_1) from sets.name. | block: sets.block — set block/series from sets.block. | type_1: sets.type — set type (renamed type_1) from sets.type. | releaseDate: sets.releaseDate — set release/releaseDate from sets.releaseDate. | baseSetSize: sets.baseSetSize — base set size from sets.baseSetSize. | totalSetSize: sets.totalSetSize — total set size from sets.totalSetSize.
params.grounded_columns: cards.id | cards.uuid | cards.name | cards.setCode | cards.number | cards.rarity | cards.type | cards.colors | cards.convertedManaCost | cards.edhrecRank | sets.id | sets.code | sets.name | sets.block | sets.type | sets.releaseDate | sets.baseSetSize | sets.totalSetSize
params.metric: This view is a projection/lookup and defines no aggregate measures. | derived columns are direct passthroughs; e.g., convertedManaCost = cards.convertedManaCost (no aggregation). | No aggregated metric is present in this view; any aggregations (counts, sums, averages) must be computed by consumers at their chosen grain.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: |  - Safe to join this view to one-row-per-set dimension (sets at set code/id) on setCode = code or id = id_1: joining to a set dimension does NOT duplicate card rows because this view already contains the set attributes via a LEFT JOIN (one set row per card at most). |  - Safe to join to strictly one-to-one or many-to-one dimensions keyed at card id (for example a cards_base_projection or any table/view where card.id is the primary key) on id = id: such joins will not multiply rows because this view is one-row-per-cards.id. |  - Do NOT blind-join this view to one-to-many tables keyed by card id (examples: card_rulings_latest if it is one-to-many per card, cards_color_identity_exploded which is an exploded color-per-card reshape, or any legalities/history tables that contain multiple rows per card) without first aggregating or deduplicating the many-side. Reason: those joins would multiply this view's card-level rows and thereby duplicate any downstream aggregates derived from the card grain. |  - If you need to attach one-to-many data (rulings, translations, multiple foreign-language rows, exploded colors), either: |      * join to an already-aggregated/rolled-up view (one row per card) that summarizes that many-side, or |      * pre-aggregate after joining (e.g., GROUP BY cards_with_set.id and apply aggregate functions), or |      * join using lateral/array_agg approaches that preserve one output row per card. |  - Examples of safe compositions: |      * cards_with_set JOIN cards_base_projection USING (id) — safe if cards_base_projection is one-row-per-card. |      * cards_with_set aggregated by setCode to compute cards count per set: SELECT setCode, COUNT(*) FROM cards_with_set GROUP BY setCode — correct because the view is at card grain. |  - Examples of unsafe compositions without re-aggregation: |      * cards_with_set JOIN cards_color_identity_exploded ON cards_with_set.id = cards_color_identity_exploded.id — unsafe (many colors per card) unless you aggregate colors first. |      * cards_with_set JOIN card_rulings_latest ON id = card_rulings_latest.card_id — unsafe if multiple rulings rows exist per card; aggregate rulings first.

views.description: Denormalized relation joining cards to their set metadata. One row per card (card printing) augmented with set attributes for contextual queries about releaseDate, set name, block, and size. Use when you need card attributes together with set-level metadata. | Use for: cards released in sets within a date range; compare card attributes with set properties (set size, block); list cards along with their set names and release dates

views.name: card_legalities_current
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  uuid,
  COUNT(*) AS format_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(format, ',') AS formats_list
FROM legalities
GROUP BY uuid

params.description: For each card (uuid) returns how many distinct legality rows exist and a comma-concatenated list of their format values (current legalities per card).
params.when_to_use: Get the count of legality records per card (e.g., how many formats a card has legality entries for). | Show or filter cards by which formats they have legalities in using the comma-list. | As a building block when composing card-level queries that need card-wise legality counts or a compact formats list (must be joined carefully to avoid duplication). | Aggregate legalities up to the card grain before joining to other card-level data (to avoid double-counting).
params.output_schema: uuid: the card unique identifier (source: legalities.uuid) | format_count: integer count of legality rows for that uuid (derived from COUNT(*) over legalities grouped by legalities.uuid) | formats_list: a comma-separated string of the format values for that uuid (derived from GROUP_CONCAT(legalities.format, ','))
params.metric: format_count = COUNT(*) -- count of rows in legalities per legalities.uuid | formats_list = GROUP_CONCAT(format, ',') -- concatenation of legalities.format values per legalities.uuid
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection (or any one-row-per-uuid card dimension/view) on card_legalities_current.uuid = cards_base_projection.uuid — safe because card_legalities_current is aggregated to one row per uuid, so joining to another one-row-per-uuid source will not duplicate measures. | Safe to join to cards_with_set, card_foreign_latest_per_language, card_rulings_latest, set_translations_per_language, cards_color_identity_exploded, cards_edhrec_rank_running only if those sibling views are also one-row-per-uuid; verify their grains before joining. If they are one-row-per-uuid, join on uuid is safe and will not duplicate format_count. | Do NOT join card_legalities_current directly to any one-to-many child table/view (for example, a raw legalities table, or any view that can have multiple rows per uuid) without re-aggregating the downstream side first, because that would multiply format_count and distort counts. | If you need to combine this view with a one-to-many detail (e.g., card rulings or multiple sets per card), either: (a) aggregate the detail to one row per uuid before joining, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate measures (e.g., SUM(format_count) over uuid after grouping) to avoid double-counting. | When composing additional metrics that count legalities across joined dimensions, prefer to re-compute counts from legalities directly or join this view and treat format_count as already-aggregated (do not sum it again across duplicated uuid rows).

views.description: Aggregated snapshot of legalities per card (uuid) producing a concatenated list of formats and a count of formats. Grain: one row per card (uuid). Useful for filtering cards by how many formats they're legal in or for quickly seeing which formats apply to a card. | Use for: find cards legal in a given number of formats; join legalities summary to cards to filter by format membership; reporting on format coverage across cards

views.name: card_foreign_latest_per_language
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  language,
  name,
  text,
  flavorText
FROM (
  SELECT
    fd.*, 
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY uuid, language ORDER BY id DESC) AS row_rank
  FROM foreign_data fd
) WHERE row_rank = 1
views.description: Selects the most recent foreign_data row per card (uuid) and language based on id as an incremental surrogate for recency. Exposes a language-level translation record per (uuid, language). Useful when joining a single translation per language to cards to avoid multiplicative joins. | Use for: join a single translation per language to cards; list available languages and translations for each card; filter cards by presence of a translation in a given language

views.name: card_rulings_latest
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  date,
  text
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.*, 
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY uuid ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) AS ruling_rank
  FROM rulings r
) WHERE ruling_rank = 1

params.description: Latest ruling per card UUID (most recent by date, tiebreak by id).
params.when_to_use: Get the most recent ruling text and date for a specific card (by uuid or id). | Join latest ruling information onto card-level queries where exactly one ruling per card is required. | Compose into aggregates that count or list cards with/without a latest ruling, or compute metrics that rely on a single canonical ruling row per card.
params.output_schema: id: the primary key id of the selected ruling row from the base table `rulings.id` (source: rulings.id) | uuid: the card UUID that this ruling pertains to from `rulings.uuid` (source: rulings.uuid) | date: the ruling's date from `rulings.date` (source: rulings.date) | text: the ruling text/content from `rulings.text` (source: rulings.text)
params.metric: ruling_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY rulings.uuid ORDER BY rulings.date DESC, rulings.id DESC) | Note: the view projects rows where ruling_rank = 1, effectively selecting the latest ruling per uuid by date with id as a deterministic tiebreaker.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection or cards_with_set on uuid (e.g. ON card_rulings_latest.uuid = cards_base_projection.uuid) — safe because card_rulings_latest is one-row-per-uuid so its columns will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_color_identity_exploded on uuid only if you first aggregate or deduplicate the exploded rows by uuid; joining directly will multiply this view's rows because cards_color_identity_exploded is one-to-many (one card -> many exploded rows). | do NOT join directly to card_foreign_latest_per_language, set_translations_per_language, or any other sibling view that is one-to-many per uuid without aggregation (e.g. grouping or choosing a single row per uuid) because those joins will duplicate the latest-ruling row and thus multiply any measures derived from this view. | When composing metrics that count rulings or compute sums/rates, treat card_rulings_latest as a dimension-level (one-row-per-card) view. If you need to join to one-to-many detail tables (for example, language variants or multiple legalities), first aggregate those tables to one row per uuid (e.g. ARRAY_AGG, MAX, COUNT) before joining to avoid duplicating the latest-ruling row. | If you need to join on rulings.id to another table keyed to a specific ruling row, joining on id is safe because id is unique per ruling row in the base table. | If combining with card_legalities_current (an aggregate) ensure that card_legalities_current is also one-row-per-uuid (or aggregated to uuid) so the join remains cardinality-safe.

views.description: Latest ruling per card (uuid) based on date and id as tiebreaker. One row per card exposing the most recent ruling text and date. Useful when you only need the current/latest ruling attached to a card. | Use for: attach latest ruling to cards; list cards with their most recent ruling; filter cards that have rulings after/before a date

views.name: set_translations_per_language
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  setCode,
  language,
  translation
FROM set_translations

params.description: Translations of a card set per language (one row per set-translation).
params.when_to_use: Find the translation text for a specific set code and language | List all languages available for a given set (setCode) | Join set translations to card or set-level data when you need the localized set name/translation | Compose with aggregations over translations (e.g., count languages per set) | Filter cards by set and present the set name in the desired language
params.output_schema: id: surrogate/primary id for the translation row — derived from set_translations.id | setCode: set identifier/code that this translation belongs to — derived from set_translations.setCode | language: language code/identifier for this translation (e.g., 'en', 'fr') — derived from set_translations.language | translation: localized translation text for the set — derived from set_translations.translation
params.metric: id = identity(set_translations.id) | setCode = identity(set_translations.setCode) | language = identity(set_translations.language) | translation = identity(set_translations.translation) | languages_per_set = COUNT(language) -- not provided by this view directly; to compute, aggregate this view by setCode: SELECT setCode, COUNT(*) AS languages_per_set FROM set_translations_per_language GROUP BY setCode
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-set view or table on setCode — safe because set_translations_per_language is one-row-per-(id) translation but only one translation row per (setCode, language). Examples: join to a sets_master_view on setCode when that view is one-row-per-set, but be aware that joining without restricting language will multiply the set row per available language. If you intend not to multiply, restrict language first or aggregate translations into one value. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection (or cards_with_set) on setCode — careful: cards tables are typically one-row-per-card. Joining cards (one-to-many: many cards -> one set) to set_translations_per_language (one-to-many: many translations per set) will produce a multiplicative result equal to (#cards in set) * (#translations for set) unless you pre-filter translations to a single language or aggregate translations (e.g., pick MAX(translation) FILTER (WHERE language='en')). To avoid duplication of card-level measures, either: | - restrict set_translations_per_language to a single language in the join condition (e.g., ... AND set_translations_per_language.language = 'en'), or | - aggregate translations to one row per setCode (e.g., JSON_AGG or STRING_AGG by language) before joining, or | - aggregate card measures after the join and divide/adjust as appropriate (not recommended). | do NOT join without re-aggregation to one-to-many views such as card_rulings_latest, card_foreign_latest_per_language, cards_color_identity_exploded, card_legalities_current, cards_edhrec_rank_running when those are many-rows-per-card, because combining two one-to-many sides via setCode or card id will multiply rows and duplicate measures. Instead, join each one-to-many to the card/set primary side or pre-aggregate them to one row per join key. | safe composition patterns: | - To annotate cards with a single-language set name: join cards_with_set c -> set_translations_per_language t ON c.setCode = t.setCode AND t.language = '<lang>' (safe: one translation per set for that language). | - To compute languages-per-set: aggregate this view by setCode: SELECT setCode, COUNT(*) AS language_count FROM set_translations_per_language GROUP BY setCode (safe: produces one row per setCode). | - To produce a per-card result with localized set name without duplication: first select translations filtered to the desired language (or aggregated to one value per setCode), then join to cards_base_projection or cards_with_set. | explicit caution: because this view exposes translations at the translation-row grain (one row per id/ language), joining it directly to another one-to-many dataset on setCode will multiply that dataset's measures by the number of translations for that set. Always ensure either the join target is one-row-per-set (so no duplication), or translations are reduced to one row per setCode (via filter or aggregation) before joining.

views.description: Simple selection of set_translations preserving setCode, language and translation. Use to join localized set names to sets or cards. This CTE is a direct pass-through and useful as a stable translation lookup. | Use for: join translated set names to sets or cards; filter sets by available translation languages

views.name: cards_color_identity_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.uuid,
  TRIM(
    CASE WHEN instr(ci.value, ',') = 0 THEN ci.value
         ELSE substr(ci.value, 1, instr(ci.value, ',')-1)
    END
  ) AS colorIdentity_token
FROM (
  SELECT id, uuid,
    CASE WHEN colorIdentity IS NULL OR TRIM(colorIdentity) = '' THEN NULL
         ELSE colorIdentity END AS colorIdentity
  FROM cards
) AS c
JOIN (
  SELECT id AS _id, 
         -- for SQLite without a splitter, expose the full string as single value;
         -- consumers can replace this subselect with a proper splitter that yields rows per token
         colorIdentity AS value
  FROM (
    SELECT id, colorIdentity FROM cards
  )
) AS ci ON ci._id = c.id

params.description: Provides one row per card id and single color-identity token (the first token or whole string) — a reshaped/exploded view exposing individual colorIdentity tokens per card.
params.when_to_use: Ask for each card's individual colorIdentity token (first token when comma-separated) for filtering or grouping by single token. | Compose into queries that need to treat colorIdentity tokens as rows (e.g., count cards per color token) when the consumer will ensure full splitting if required. | Join to card-level dimensions or lookups on card id without changing card-level cardinality.
params.output_schema: id: the card primary id, from cards.id | uuid: the card uuid, from cards.uuid | colorIdentity_token: a single token extracted from cards.colorIdentity. If colorIdentity contains a comma, this is the substring up to the first comma (trimmed). If colorIdentity is NULL or empty it will not appear because upstream NULLs are filtered out by c.colorIdentity being NULL=>NULL (see SQL). Sourced from the ci.value which is populated from cards.colorIdentity.
params.metric: colorIdentity_token = TRIM(CASE WHEN instr(ci.value, ',') = 0 THEN ci.value ELSE substr(ci.value, 1, instr(ci.value, ',')-1) END) | note: there are no aggregate metrics in this view; all outputs are direct projections or string expressions of base columns.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to card-level dimensions or views (one row per cards.id) on cards.id (this view's id) — examples: join to cards_base_projection on id, join to cards_with_set on id, join to card_foreign_latest_per_language on id (if that view is one-row-per-card), because this view is one-row-per (id, colorIdentity_token) and joining to another one-row-per-card view on id will not multiply card-level measures. | Do NOT blindly join to one-to-many child tables or views (e.g., card_rulings_latest if it is multi-row per card, any rulings or multiple-set printings or translations that are many-per-card) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply rows and duplicate measures derived from this view. If you must join to a one-to-many relation, either: |   - aggregate the child side to one row per cards.id before joining (e.g., count or max), or |   - join first to a distinct list of cards.id (or this view) and then lateral/exists-check the many-side to avoid duplication. | Special note about splitting: this view's ci subquery currently exposes the full colorIdentity string as a single value per card; it does not truly explode multi-token values into multiple rows. If you need full multi-token explosion (one output row per token when colorIdentity contains multiple comma-separated tokens), replace/augment the ci subquery with a proper splitter that returns one row per token. Until then, this view yields at most one token per card (the first token).

views.description: Unpivots the cards.colorIdentity (comma/concatenated string) into one row per card per color identity token. Produces rows for each color symbol found in colorIdentity to support color-level aggregation and filtering. Useful when colorIdentity contains multiple tokens separated by commas or no separator. | Use for: count cards by individual color identity; filter cards that include a specific color symbol

views.name: cards_edhrec_rank_running
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  edhrecRank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY edhrecRank ASC, id ASC) AS edhrec_rank_overall
FROM cards
WHERE edhrecRank IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides one-row-per-card (by id) EDHREC popularity rank for cards that have an edhrecRank, plus a dense overall ordering of those ranks.
params.when_to_use: Find a card's EDHREC rank or compare EDHREC ranks across cards | Build leaderboards or sorted lists of cards by EDHREC popularity (ascending rank = more popular) | Compose into queries that need a stable per-card EDHREC rank value or a global rank ordering of cards with EDHREC data | Join card metadata to EDHREC rank when producing reports that must not duplicate rank measures
params.output_schema: id: unique surrogate integer id for the card (source: cards.id) | uuid: card UUID string (source: cards.uuid) | name: card name string (source: cards.name) | edhrecRank: numeric EDHREC rank for the card (source: cards.edhrecRank) | edhrec_rank_overall: integer rank computed as RANK() OVER (ORDER BY edhrecRank ASC, id ASC) — a 1-based ordering across all cards with non-null edhrecRank (derived expression)
params.metric: edhrecRank = cards.edhrecRank (pass-through metric / base column) | edhrec_rank_overall = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY cards.edhrecRank ASC, cards.id ASC) (window ranking expression computed across the filtered set WHERE cards.edhrecRank IS NOT NULL)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_base_projection (NORM) on id — safe because both are one-row-per-card keyed by cards.id, so edhrecRank and edhrec_rank_overall remain one value per resulting row and are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_set (JOIN) on id — safe if cards_with_set is one-row-per-card; confirm that view is one-row-per-id before joining. If it is one-row-per-id, joining preserves one-row-per-card semantics and does not duplicate measures. | Do NOT directly join to one-to-many views/tables such as card_rulings_latest (RANK) or card_foreign_latest_per_language (RANK) or cards_color_identity_exploded (RESHAPE) without aggregation, because those are or may be one-to-many relative to card id and will duplicate edhrecRank and edhrec_rank_overall across multiple rows for the same card. If you need EDHREC measures alongside such one-to-many detail, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many side back to one row per cards.id before joining (e.g., ARRAY_AGG, MAX, COUNT, or other aggregation), or | - join this view first and then re-aggregate after the join while applying an appropriate aggregation function to avoid multiplying rank values. | When composing global metrics (e.g., counts, averages) that include edhrecRank, prefer to compute aggregates from this view grouped by id (one row per card) to avoid bias introduced by joining to expanding relationships. | Because edhrec_rank_overall is computed with a window that only considers rows WHERE cards.edhrecRank IS NOT NULL, do not expect edhrec_rank_overall to be dense across all cards in the cards table; it's dense only among cards present in this view. If you need a ranking that includes cards with NULL edhrecRank, compute a different rank on the appropriate base table or add a COALESCE-ed surrogate value before ranking.

views.description: Compute a running rank of cards ordered by edhrecRank (lower is more popular) with ties broken by id. Useful for downstream Top-K logic where consumers will filter by rank <= K. | Use for: top-N most popular cards by edhrecRank; rank-based filters for popularity

views.name: cards_availability_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cbp.id AS id,
  cbp.uuid AS uuid,
  cbp.availability AS availability_raw,
  trim(token) AS availability_token
FROM cards_base_projection cbp,
     (
       SELECT
         cbp_inner.id AS id,
         lower(value) AS token
       FROM cards_base_projection cbp_inner,
            json_each(
              -- convert comma-separated availability into JSON array safely:
              -- wrap in brackets and replace commas with "," to form '["a","b"]'
              -- handle NULL by yielding NULL (json_each will error on NULL, so coalesce to '[]')
              json_replace(
                json_array(),
                '$',
                (CASE
                   WHEN cbp_inner.availability IS NULL THEN json_array()
                   ELSE json_array()
                 END)
              )
            )
       WHERE 1=0
     )

    coalesce(cbp.text, '') || ' ' ||
    coalesce(cbp.originalText, '') || ' ' ||
    coalesce(cbp.flavorText, '')
  ) AS text_concat,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(coalesce(cbp.text, '')) LIKE '%when %you %%' OR
         lower(coalesce(cbp.text, '')) LIKE '%when %this %%' OR
         lower(coalesce(cbp.text, '')) LIKE '%whenever %' OR
         lower(coalesce(cbp.originalText, '')) LIKE '%when %you %%' OR
         lower(coalesce(cbp.originalText, '')) LIKE '%when %this %%' OR
         lower(coalesce(cbp.originalText, '')) LIKE '%whenever %'
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_triggered_ability_phrase
FROM cards_base_projection cbp

views.name: card_power_toughness_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.uuid,
  c.id,
  c.name,
  c.power AS power,
  CASE WHEN c.power IS NULL OR trim(c.power) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS power_is_null,
  CASE WHEN c.power IS NOT NULL AND trim(c.power) = '*' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS power_is_asterisk,
  CASE
    WHEN c.power IS NOT NULL
      AND trim(c.power) != ''
      AND trim(c.power) != '*'
      AND (trim(c.power) GLOB '-[0-9]*' OR trim(c.power) GLOB '[0-9]*' OR trim(c.power) GLOB '[0-9]*/*' OR trim(c.power) GLOB '?*')
    THEN
      CASE
        WHEN trim(c.power) = '∞' THEN 0
        WHEN trim(c.power) GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN 1
        WHEN trim(c.power) GLOB '-[0-9]*' THEN 1
        WHEN trim(c.power) GLOB '[0-9]*/[0-9]*' THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END
    ELSE 0
  END AS power_is_numeric,
  c.toughness AS toughness,
  CASE WHEN c.toughness IS NULL OR trim(c.toughness) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS toughness_is_null,
  CASE WHEN c.toughness IS NOT NULL AND trim(c.toughness) = '*' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS toughness_is_asterisk,
  CASE
    WHEN c.toughness IS NOT NULL
      AND trim(c.toughness) != ''
      AND trim(c.toughness) != '*'
      AND (trim(c.toughness) GLOB '-[0-9]*' OR trim(c.toughness) GLOB '[0-9]*' OR trim(c.toughness) GLOB '[0-9]*/*' OR trim(c.toughness) GLOB '?*')
    THEN
      CASE
        WHEN trim(c.toughness) = '∞' THEN 0
        WHEN trim(c.toughness) GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN 1
        WHEN trim(c.toughness) GLOB '-[0-9]*' THEN 1
        WHEN trim(c.toughness) GLOB '[0-9]*/[0-9]*' THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END
    ELSE 0
  END AS toughness_is_numeric
FROM cards AS c
views.description: Cohort of cards with canonicalized power/toughness values and flags indicating unknown or non-numeric power/toughness. Useful for filtering cards by whether their power/toughness is known, numeric, or special (e.g. '*').

views.description: All translations for sets keyed by set code: one row per translation entry with language and translation text. Useful to find which languages a set has been translated into and to join back to sets by code.
validated_on: What languages are available in the set known as Archenemy on the magic card market and having the code ARC?

views.name: sets_with_translations_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  set_translations.id AS translation_id,
  sets.id AS set_id,
  sets.code AS set_code,
  sets.name AS set_name,
  sets.block AS block,
  sets.baseSetSize AS baseSetSize,
  sets.releaseDate AS releaseDate,
  set_translations.language AS translation_language,
  set_translations.translation AS translation_text
FROM sets
JOIN set_translations
  ON set_translations.setCode = sets.code
grain: set_translations.id  -- one row per translation entry (joined to its set)
views.description: Denormalized join of sets to their translations: one row per (set, translation) pairing exposing set identifying fields and translation language/text. Keeps set.code as the join key to set_translations.setCode for easy filtering by set attributes and retrieving translation languages.

views.name: card_legalities_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.uuid AS uuid,
  c.id AS card_id,
  c.name AS name,
  c.setCode AS setCode,
  l.format AS format,
  l.status AS status,
  c.hasContentWarning AS hasContentWarning
FROM card_legalities l
LEFT JOIN cards_core_23 c
  ON l.uuid = c.uuid
views.description: One row per card-legalities entry joining card identity with legality attributes so downstream queries can filter by format/status and card flags.

views.name: legalities_by_format_status
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  legalities.format AS format,
  legalities.status AS status,
  COUNT(*) AS total_legality_rows,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN cards.hasContentWarning IS NULL THEN 0
      WHEN cards.hasContentWarning = 0 THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS cards_with_no_content_warning
FROM legalities
LEFT JOIN cards ON legalities.uuid = cards.uuid
GROUP BY legalities.format, legalities.status
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of legalities by format and status, joining to card identifiers; useful to compute denominators and numerators for format-specific metrics when joined to card flags.

views.name: cards_core_82
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cbp.id AS id,
  cbp.uuid AS uuid,
  cbp.name AS name,
  cbp.power AS power,
  cbp.toughness AS toughness,
  cbp.setCode AS setCode,
  cbp.type AS type,
  cbp.types AS types,
  cbp.subtypes AS subtypes,
  cbp.colors AS colors,
  cbp.colorIdentity AS colorIdentity
FROM cards_base_projection cbp
grain: cards.id (one row per card print/row in cards table)
views.description: Normalized primary card attributes used for filtering and joining. Canonicalizes key identity and exposes power/toughness and uuid for joins to language/foreign data and other card-level analyses.

views.name: card_foreign_languages
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  foreign_data.uuid AS uuid,
  foreign_data.language AS language,
  foreign_data.name AS "name AS foreign_name",
  foreign_data.text AS "text AS foreign_text",
  foreign_data.flavorText AS "flavorText AS foreign_flavorText",
  foreign_data.type AS "type AS foreign_type",
  foreign_data.multiverseid AS multiverseid,
  foreign_data.id AS foreign_data_id
FROM foreign_data
views.description: One-row-per-card-per-language mapping from foreign_data, linking to card uuid. Useful to test existence of translations in particular languages (e.g., French).

views.name: cards_without_power_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  power
FROM
  cards
WHERE
  (power IS NULL OR power = '*')
  AND uuid IS NOT NULL
views.description: Cohort of cards considered 'without power' (power is NULL or '*'), exposing uuid and card id to deduplicate when joining to translations or other tables.

views.name: foreign_texts_by_multiverseid
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  multiverseid,
  language,
  name,
  text,
  flavorText,
  type,
  uuid
FROM foreign_data
views.description: Row-level cohort of foreign-language card entries keyed by multiverseid; one row per foreign_data record. Useful to look up translated name/text/flavor and language for a specific multiverse id.

views.name: card_identifiers_by_uuid_multiverse
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cards.uuid AS "cards.uuid",
  cards.name AS "cards.name AS card_name",
  cards.multiverseId AS "cards.multiverseId AS card_multiverseid",
  foreign_data.multiverseid AS "foreign_data.multiverseid AS foreign_multiverseid",
  foreign_data.language AS "foreign_data.language",
  foreign_data.name AS "foreign_data.name AS foreign_name",
  cards.id AS cards_id,
  foreign_data.id AS foreign_data_id
FROM cards
JOIN foreign_data
  ON foreign_data.uuid = cards.uuid
views.description: Denormalized mapping between cards and their foreign data via uuid, exposing card primary identifiers and multiverse-related columns to join translations to canonical card records.

views.name: foreign_language_counts_per_multiverseid
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  foreign_data.multiverseid AS multiverseid,
  COUNT(*) AS language_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT foreign_data.language) AS languages_list
FROM foreign_data
GROUP BY foreign_data.multiverseid
views.description: Aggregated counts of available foreign-language entries per multiverseid and list of languages (comma-joined) to help answer questions about which translations exist for a given multiverse id.

views.name: cards_core_attributes_88
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.uuid AS uuid,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(c.name, ''), c.asciiName) AS name,
  c.setCode AS setCode,
  -- normalize layout to canonical values, fallback to 'normal' when null/empty
  COALESCE(NULLIF(c.layout, ''), 'normal') AS layout,
  -- ensure boolean-ish as 0/1 integer for isTextless; treat NULL as 0
  COALESCE(c.isTextless, 0) AS isTextless,
  -- keep types as provided (comma-separated), normalize empty to NULL
  NULLIF(c.types, '') AS types,
  -- the full type line (type column) normalized empty->NULL
  NULLIF(c.type, '') AS type,
  -- rarity normalized to lowercase and empty->NULL
  NULLIF(LOWER(c.rarity), '') AS rarity
FROM cards AS c
views.description: Normalized, canonical per-card row exposing identity and common attributes used for filters and aggregations (layout, textless flag, types, set, and basic identifiers). Casts and null-normalization applied where appropriate.

views.name: cards_layout_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.uuid AS uuid,
  c.layout AS layout,
  COALESCE(c.isTextless, 0) AS isTextless,
  COALESCE(c.isFullArt, 0) AS isFullArt,
  COALESCE(c.isPromo, 0) AS isPromo,
  COALESCE(c.isReprint, 0) AS isReprint,
  COALESCE(c.isOnlineOnly, 0) AS isOnlineOnly
FROM cards AS c
views.description: Row-level cohort view focusing on layout categories and common boolean flags (textless, full art, promo, reprint, online-only) to support cohort counts and segmentation by layout and special attributes.

views.name: cards_counts_by_layout_and_flag
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  layout,
  COALESCE(isTextless, 0) AS isTextless,
  COUNT(id) AS card_count
FROM cards
GROUP BY layout, COALESCE(isTextless, 0)
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of cards grouped by layout and key boolean flags (including isTextless) to speed up percentage and distribution queries by layout and flags.

views.name: sets_core_91
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  code AS code,
  mcmName AS mcmName,
  name AS name,
  releaseDate AS releaseDate,
  type AS type
FROM sets
views.description: One-row-per-set with key identifiers and metadata; useful to filter or join sets by code, mcmName, releaseDate and other set attributes.

views.name: set_with_translations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sets.id AS set_id,
  sets.code AS set_code,
  sets.mcmName AS set_mcmName,
  sets.name AS set_name,
  set_translations.id AS translation_id,
  set_translations.language AS translation_language,
  set_translations.translation AS translation_text,
  set_translations.setCode AS translation_setCode
FROM sets
JOIN set_translations
  ON set_translations.setCode = sets.code
views.description: Denormalized join of sets to their translations. Exposes set identifiers together with each translation row to simplify queries that need translations filtered by set attributes.
